focus: fleet orchestration over all cannons (dashboards, balancing, trigger tasks that fire other cannons)
hydrator_prompt: Keep the OVERMIND pool at >=10 waiting tasks focused on orchestrating the OTHER cannons (fortress, conduit, ledger, relay, bastion, supermax). This cannon watches and tunes the fleet; it also owns TRIGGER tasks that enqueue work into other pools or fire other cannons. Check depth: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM task_pool WHERE instance_target='overmind' AND status='waiting'. If <10, generate 6 specific IMPLEMENTATION or TRIGGER tasks. Priority 20-60. Insert, re-queue yourself priority 1, log pool.hydrated.

tasks.name: fleet-dashboard
tasks.prompt: Build a single fleet dashboard (HTML in R2 or a worker route, auto-refresh) showing every cannon side by side: waiting/running/completed/failed counts, last fire time, chain depth today, pause state, and last 5 events per instance. Query task_pool + events + cannon_state grouped by instance_target/source. One screen = whole fleet. Document the queries.

tasks.name: pool-balancer
tasks.prompt: Build a pool balancer: detect a starving cannon (waiting near 0 while others are deep) or a stalled one (no cannon.fired event in >20 min) and recommend/act. For starvation, it may enqueue a hydrator nudge; for a stall, it may fire the cannon (see fire-trigger task). Log every balancing action to events. Document the thresholds.

tasks.name: fleet-quality-scoring
tasks.prompt: Score completed tasks across ALL cannons: completeness, time-vs-estimate, retry/failure rate by category and instance. Surface systemic issues (a cannon whose estimates are always low, a category that always fails). Write a weekly fleet quality report to R2 and post a summary to #cannon-ops via RELAY. Document the scoring method.

tasks.name: trigger-cross-pool-enqueue
tasks.prompt: Build the CROSS-POOL ENQUEUE trigger primitive: a task whose whole job is to INSERT tasks into ANOTHER cannon's pool based on a condition. Example: when FORTRESS completes 'dmarc-stage3-reject', enqueue a 'verify mail deliverability end-to-end' task into RELAY's pool. Implement a reusable helper: enqueue(target_instance, task) that writes to task_pool with the right instance_target. Log a 'trigger.enqueued' event. Document how to define new cross-pool rules.

tasks.name: trigger-fire-cannon
tasks.prompt: Build the FIRE-CANNON trigger primitive: a task that calls create_scheduled_task to kick a specific cannon's next fire IMMEDIATELY (jump the interval) instead of waiting. Use for: a starving/stalled cannon, or a dependency just cleared and downstream work should run now. Guard against firing a paused or runaway-tripped cannon. Log 'trigger.fired' with target + reason. This is orchestration, not research — it triggers other things. Document usage and guards.

tasks.name: fleet-cost-throughput
tasks.prompt: Aggregate cost/throughput across the fleet from the events table: salvos/hour, tasks/hour, hot-streak vs cooldown ratio, per-cannon burn rate, and (if AI Gateway logging is wired) token/$ spend per cannon. Render trends. This tells you which cannon is actually producing and which is spinning. Write to the fleet dashboard and a daily digest. Document the metrics.

tasks.name: global-circuit-breaker
tasks.prompt: Implement a GLOBAL circuit breaker in cannon_state: if multiple cannons cross a failure threshold in the same window (e.g. >=5 task_failed events across the fleet in 15 min), set every <instance>_paused='true' and log 'fleet.circuit_open'. Auto-clear after a cooldown when failure rate drops, logging 'fleet.circuit_closed'. This stops a systemic problem (e.g. a leaked/rotated secret) from burning credits fleet-wide. Document thresholds and the manual override.

tasks.name: dependency-graph
tasks.prompt: Build a cross-cannon dependency graph using the depends_on column + cross-pool triggers: encode real ordering (FORTRESS secrets before CONDUIT wiring; CONDUIT AI Gateway before RELAY's AI panel; LEDGER R2-system-of-record before knowledge sync). Visualize it and let OVERMIND respect it when firing/enqueuing. Document the graph and how new dependencies are added.
